patch.value:
## Problem
Storage carries a format_version field and migration primitives are planned, but no test answers the practical questions: what does today's build do with a workspace written by last month's build, what does last month's build do with today's, and what happens when two such agents merge branches.

## Approach
A matrix job that installs prior published releases, generates representative workspaces with them, then runs the current build's read, mutate, validate, merge, and history-verify paths against those workspaces — and the mirror direction using the current build as writer.

## Field preservation
The critical invariant is that an older reader must not destroy fields it does not understand. Round-trip preservation of unknown fields is what makes a staggered fleet safe, and it must be asserted explicitly.

## Boundary
Not schema migration itself, which is owned separately. This proves the compatibility window; migrations move workspaces across it.
Cross-version workspace compatibility matrix: prove that workspaces written by older and newer pm releases stay readable and mergeable

The matrix covers at least the previous two release lines writing and the current build reading, plus the reverse direction; Forward-incompatible reads fail loudly with an actionable error rather than silently misparsing or dropping fields; Backward-compatible reads preserve unknown fields on round-trip so an older reader cannot destroy a newer writer's data; Merge drivers are exercised across version skew, not only within one version; The declared compatibility window is documented and the matrix fails when the code drifts from the declaration
A workspace is never bricked or silently misread by a version skew between agents
Thousands of agents on many machines will not run the same pm build. Format skew between writers and readers is therefore the normal case, not an edge case, and nothing currently tests it.
Protects the durability promise across upgrades and makes the storage format_version policy in the GA contract enforceable rather than declarative.
A CI matrix writes workspaces with previous releases, reads and mutates them with the current build, and asserts defined behaviour in both directions including refusal where refusal is correct.

The format_version field exists and migrations are planned, but there is no test proving what happens when a newer writer meets an older reader — the exact situation a staggered agent fleet creates daily.
